attacks.claim: The plan sends customer documents, chunks, embeddings and prompts to Nimbus and stores them in Vector Store in us-east-2 (US) while the stated constraint is EU-only processing and storage under customer DPAs. Week 2 re-embeds the full 41M-chunk corpus into that US-hosted store, which breaches the DPA constraint and is hard to undo once data is there.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." vs. constraint: "all customer documents and anything derived from them (chunks, embeddings, prompts) must be processed and stored in the EU"

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is claimed for the Inference API, but the ZDR addendum is not shown to cover Vector Store, embed-3 ingestion, or the public-preview service, so retention terms for stored embeddings and chunks are unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." — ABSENT: any statement that NMB-ZDR-2291 covers Vector Store or embeddings, and no sub-processor/DPA update is mentioned.

attacks.claim: Quality parity is not established. The plan removes the 4,100-case regression suite as a release gate and moves it to week 6+, after the week-4 cutover to all tenants, so a model change reaches production without the agreed gate. The 25-question blind comparison cannot support 'parity or better'.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover." vs. constraint: "the 4,100-case regression eval suite is the release gate for any model change."

attacks.claim: The quality claim rests on a sample of 25 support-inbox questions judged by two lawyers, which is too small and unrepresentative to show parity for legal QA. The LoRA-to-system-prompt conversion, which changes behaviour per practice area, is also unvalidated.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox... Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3." — ABSENT: per-practice-area results, accuracy vs. ground truth, and any evaluation of the system-prompt replacement for LoRA adapters.

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly destroys the rollback path before cutover: the A100 reservation is released and fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters are deleted, while tenants are still on vLLM until week 4 and the Nimbus migration is not yet proven. A failed cutover or a Nimbus outage leaves no working fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" followed by "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus" and "Week 6+: regression suite run".

attacks.claim: Week 5 deletes pgvector, vLLM manifests and the GPU node pool from Terraform before the post-cutover regression run and any rollback window are complete. Returning to self-hosting would then require rebuilding the stack.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform." with "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: The plan replaces a self-hosted model (Llama-3.1-70B with LoRA weights) and self-hosted pgvector with single-vendor managed services. Exit cost is high: model weights and adapters are deleted in week 3 and the vector store is in preview, so no self-hosting or migration-out path is kept.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"; "remove pgvector"; "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector"

attacks.claim: Generation is on a single provider with no documented fallback or second provider.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any fallback provider or contingency for Nimbus outage or deprecation.

attacks.claim: The rate-limit headroom is thin and unverified. Peak demand is 40 req/s against a 120 req/s contracted limit, which leaves no margin for retries, re-embedding bursts in week 2, or the dual-write load, and no load test is shown.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s." — ABSENT: load test results, burst behaviour, or backoff/retry policy.

attacks.claim: The vector store is in public preview, and the plan has no SLA, failure-mode analysis, or observability plan for the new managed dependencies.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: SLA, alerting, or fallback for Nimbus Inference API and Vector Store outages.

attacks.claim: The cost estimate is unverified and omits key items. Generation cost is labeled 'est.' with no token or usage basis. It also ignores re-embedding cost for 41M chunks, dual-write overhead, and the cost of running parallel stacks during weeks 2–5, while the 200k-context capability may increase per-request token spend.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.)   | $0 | $7,900" and "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)" — ABSENT: token-volume math, one-time re-embedding cost, and dual-running cost.

attacks.claim: The savings figure of $18.4k/mo is cited against a total that also includes storage and Nimbus costs, and the storage saving is applied even though the weights are deleted only after the cutover window.
attacks.evidence: "saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle" and "close out the 6.2 TB storage line"

attacks.claim: Corpus size and growth are not addressed at target scale. The plan does not state how per-tenant Vector Store collections behave with many tenants, large collection counts, or 41M-chunk indices. Latency was measured only from one week and one location.
attacks.evidence: "Collections are created per tenant"; "1,000 requests, week of 10-05" — ABSENT: tenant count, collection limits, index-size scaling tests.

attacks.claim: Tenant-scoped key isolation depends on a preview product. Data from each tenant is co-located in a US region and a preview service, which raises cross-tenant and processor exposure concerns not analyzed in the plan.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key" — ABSENT: isolation testing, sub-processor disclosure, or data residency assessment for the preview service.

attacks.claim: Keys are rotated every 30 days, but the plan doesn't say how the dual-write and tenant-scoped keys are revoked or audited, or how a leaked tenant key is contained.
attacks.evidence: "rotated every 30 days; no keys in images or env files." — ABSENT: revocation and audit procedure.

attacks.claim: Latency improved but the case for the change rests on cost and ops toil; the plan does not state a user-facing quality or latency target to validate success.
attacks.evidence: "Latency: Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods" — ABSENT: success criteria.

attacks.claim: Replacing LoRA adapters with system prompts moves per-practice behaviour into prompt text with no versioning or test coverage described, which makes regressions harder to attribute.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: No user-visible changes are described, so there is no UI risk identified.
attacks.evidence: nothing

attacks.claim: No user-facing interface changes are described, so no accessibility impact is identified.
attacks.evidence: nothing

attacks.claim: The plan is internally inconsistent: it describes the cutover as a single step across all tenants in week 4, with no staged or canary rollout, despite the risks above.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)."
